reviews.review: its a good game, but the meele weapons and meele combat are clunky, almost useless. level design are bad and if you die need to kill every simple mob because they eat 1/3 of you healt with normals shoots, so you need to run to get your souls back. get a discount and play.

On release I don't think this sold too well, it was pitched as Dark Souls with guns (which it is) and it's extreme difficulty and occasional flaw (some of the NPC animations are a little ropey, when they speak thier jaws just flap about for example) made critics give it some harsher than justified reviews. Given some time and a bit of grinding, Immortal Unchained is a great SoulsBourne homage and a great game.
Set in a distopian sci-fi universe, you start out in The Core, which serves as a very basic tutorial area and the central hub (think Firelink Shrine). From there there are 3 worlds to explore:
- Arden: A frozen surface covering a mechanical necropolis
- Veridian: Dense inhospitable jungle over rivers of lava and magma
- Apexion: The ruins of a civilisation with sprawling city scapes and decrepit urban environments
You have a huge arsenal to find of both ranged and melee weapons. The games is all about gunplay though so melee weapons are primarly a last ditch resort if you've found yourself in over your head and need to do some quick, massive damage and then run like hell. Guns come in various forms; pistols, SMG's, assault rifles, sniper rifles and launchers. There's different types of each with different attachments (silenced weapons come in handy for attacking without alerting nearby enemies), they come in different rarity from common to unique and on top of all that all weapons come in 1 of 5 flavours: Physical damage, Fire, Ice, Energy or Acid. Different enemies are resistant or vulnerable to different elements which you can generally work out by what colour they are or where in the game they are (ice world enemies are vulnerable to fire usually and so on). In most cases when you get a weapon it'll be crude and you can upgrade it 6 or 7 times to be perfect, this along with levelling up your character is the key to progressing in the game. Although you only start with one ranged and one melee weapon, you can unlock 3 additional ranged weapon slots as you progress.
Combat can take a minute to get used to (especially coming from Dark Souls) but is extremely satisfying once you get the hang of it. Click the right stick to lock onto an enemy when you are close enough and you can blast away at their centre of mass. If you don't lock on you can free aim to get head shots or blow off limbs, extremely handy when an enemy has a shield or a very powerful canon trained on your head. Blow off their gun arm and move in for the kill. Most enemies have both melee and ranged weapons too as well as a big glowing weak spot on their back so often times the best way to attack larger shielded enemies is to head shot them to weaken them, get in close, lock on, dodge the devastating melee attacks to get behind them and blast their weak spot. This combination of combat techniques is what makes it so much fun, it's not like simple FPS combat where you blast until they drop.
There's all sorts of consumables including health syringes and grenades which renew each time you spawn or reach a checkpoint and other items like ammo packs and defensive upgrades which are finite and have to be found in the world. There are 4 quick slots or you can use items directly from the inventory.
The game universe itself is massive and varied, on a par with Dark Souls in size. It's filled with secrets, shortcuts, items, chests and doors both locked and open, meaning you have to revisit areas once you have collected the required keys to get to the good stuff inside. Locked chests aren't just place holders for pickups like bits (think souls), ammo packs etc, they usually have stuff that you really want like rare weapons.
Bosses, there's a bunch and they're all over the place. There are optional bosses often sat behind those locked doors and main bosses. Wierdly the optional bosses are a lot harder than the main ones. Most of the main bosses I've been able to beat 1st attempt while the optionals have me rage quitting.
The storyline I haven't really been following to be honest. Space, prisoner, save the universe, something like that. But I've been paying attention enough to know there's some big twists and turns without spoiling it. Like Dark Souls, there's no mission log, you just have to remember what you've been told to understand what you're meant to be doing. Same with NPC's and their side quests. To make life easier, the main quest is like this: 
Escape from the prison (tutorial), go to each of the worlds and find the Nexus (a big orb) and activate it. Activating all 3 unlocks fast travel and the path forward. From there you have to explore further into each world and defeat their bosses before going head to head with the end boss.
I've gone into so much detail as the game doesn't tell you how to play it, barring the very basics, and it is a great game once you get into it. So if you give it a chance, this will give you a head start.
Definitely recommended for SoulsBourne fans, overlook a couple of little flaws and a grind up front and you'll be rewarded with an excellent 'Dark Souls with guns'.

This game is seriously unbalanced and a chore to play. If you insist I fully recommend a sniper build and go for headshots and weak spots. I enjoyed the atmosphere, the setting and the lore (what there was of it) and the story has a couple of twists at the end that I didn't see coming. But playing the game is a total chore.

Immortal Unchained has improved a lot since it first released. It received a lot of polish since then and is pretty underrated for what it is. Is it as good as Dark Souls? No. It's probably as good as The Surge, and it does a decent job of fusing a shooter with a souls-like. 
I'd give it a 7/10, but has the potential of becoming an 8 with more polish and balancing (possibly with the assistance of mods).

Don't even remember when I got this game. It's interesting and seemed kinda like it would be fun when starting. Now I'm in a glowing neon city and getting gang-banged by teleporting snipers and ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ with energy shields.  Gunplay feels like fishing for backstabs 90% of the time and although stats are laid out in an alright fashion to understand but still doesn't seem to help. I feel like I'm trying to play Mortal Shell with how much the progression doesn't seem to matter. Armor shrines replace typical armor and makes it feel more like a metroidvania game. The main direction given for the first boss after the starter boss was just fine. Veridian forest can eat the entirety of my ass. and Nexion is cancer.  Weapon drops are actually slightly useful though. Breaking down items gives you upgrade components and bits back so you can upgrade weapons. Though it feels a little weird when I'm using what is basically an AK platform auto-rifle shooting in controlled bursts and after the second round the gun is firing 45 degrees upward from where I am aiming. Basic strategy is pretty much nonexistent aside from barrel stuffing every enemy and circle jerking them with the occasional dodge until dead. I am masochistically playing this at this point just to see where the story goes. Since it has an interesting atmosphere and story, but feels like they really just don't want you to use melee aside from specific enemies... 

In all, I recommend most other souls-like games over  this title unless you get it on sale or really want something familiar yet different. Hellpoint or Code Vein are my recommendations over this game so far.

Pros
-cool weapon designs
-interesting sci-fi setting and overall aesthetic
-good sound design

Cons
-no actual progression
-filled to the top with artificial difficulty and mundane repetitive tasks
-every enemy is a bullet sponge that can stun lock, stagger, and knock you down until you expire
-bad level design that makes no sense and is designed to disorient and troll the player
-while the weapons have cool designs and there is an upgrade mechanic, it is meaningless since every enemy is an armored bullet-sponge
-not a fun game, and not even worth buying at $0.99



Yeah, this game is NOT fun. They copied Dark Souls without understanding just how deep and interconnected each mechanic is, even down to using certain weapons against certain scenario types. Aside from having to fight through lethal trash mobs to make it back to the boss when you die, back-track through each completed level to the start, the steps of Apexion where both shielded and teleporting 1-shot snipers like to gank the player character is one of many examples of how these devs really don't "get" the "souls" formula beyond a very basic depth. It's weird, because I hated alot of things about Lords of the Fallen and yet it managed to execute it's version of the souls formula way better than I:U. The Soothesayer Commander fight at Apexion is a giant troll farm of a fight and what comes after the fight is total BS. Go long range and he infinitely summons seekers (I had 8 adds on screen before I just run out of stamina dodging and shooting), go-close range and deal with his one shot swipes and energy waves that occupy 160 degrees of angle. This game is a chore mechanically and very unrewarding even when you manage to get lucky.

This is the first "souls-like" that I have ever had to take "frustration breaks" with. For all that the Souls Series does to make you feel like you are in control and add a certain graceful fluidity to your movements, this game goes the opposite direction and attempts at every opportunity to be a slow, clunky mess. The mechanics of a game like this are supposed to be a blessing, not an obstacle.

I tried so hard to find even a modicum of redeeming quality for this game, and I'd rather repeatedly bang my head into a wall than play this again. 

Update 7/5/21
After witnessing the second half of the game, I've begrudgingly consigned this game as, "a laundry list of bad choices, and all the things a "Souls-like" should never do." This game is horrendously imbalanced as if a fledgling dev just decided to try to copy the souls formula, add guns, then remove all the fun and the reasons for using guns. Reloading is absolutely stupid in this game, as you cannot sprint or dodge while reloading and if you try to dodge or sprint your reload gets cancelled. That's around 5-10 seconds in the middle of  a fight that you have to stand still and do nothing. The stun-locking is completely lop-sided, as the player character can be knocked down and infinitely stun-locked until neutralized, but enemies don't have this problem. I even witnessed an enemy running at me from a good distance like a headless chicken, meanwhile tagging me with pin-point accuracy with his dual SMGs as my puny fully upgraded "Elite Legion Assault Rifle" shot what must have been frozen peas at him at low speed. Even though I successfully shot him 20 times in the moving exchange, it did nothing to alter his aim or slow him down. His movement reminded me of the falconeer warriors from Dark Souls 2 with their janky unconnected leg movement.

The player character has no shield mechanic and there are almost no actual ways to mitigate or not take damage, but the enemies sure do, they have shields as well as ground mounted force fields that they can fire through, which makes this game very cheap.

The Souls Series has strived to maintain player agency, fluidity, and the 1/3 reward, 2/3 challenge formula, only for this game to completely break this well established concept and abuse it to constantly troll and punish the player with absolutely no incentive to continue or meaningful reward to offset the challenges that are overcome.

I'm half-way through the game and every single trash enemy can one-shot me. All my weapons are uncommon or greater and all are fully upgraded. There is no progression in this game and it would have been better if this game were never made, rather than shoddily designed and then abandoned as it is.
